what_was_done: The cli branch of launch.sh now has a `1) exit 1 ;;` case before the catch-all, so vsdd's own negative answer exits 1 silently; the crash message moved to the other codes. Test would fail without the case (it asserts empty stdout and stderr on rc 1).

EVENT_SCHEMA now admits what the launcher writes: session_id typed ['string','null'] and a ts pattern (_TS_READ_RE) admitting whole seconds as well as milliseconds; the Python writer keeps its strict millisecond form and non-empty session id (build()). Tests validate a launcher-shaped line against the schema and assert the writer's strictness.

C1 delivered: survey, checkpoint-result, delivery-data, story-unit, wave-gate-data and implement-data are now files under next/plugins/vsdd-factory/schemas/ (pending-output renamed from gate-output to match the registry id), every S_* literal in workflow-lib/prelude.js is generated by tools/build.py from its file (the hand-written composites S_REVIEW, S_FIXES, S_RULINGS, S_HOLDOUT, S_SURVEY, S_CLOSE, S_DELIVERY, S_WAVE_GATE were deleted), --check fails on drift, and check.py pins the shipped set. Each new schema ships with valid and invalid fixtures.
where: next/tools/build.py LITERAL_NAMES; next/tools/check.py schemas_are_the_single_source; next/workflow-lib/prelude.js; next/tests/unit/fixtures/schemas/

what_was_done: Settled as two schemas, as the registry already names them: gate-result.schema.json is the ordinary gate result, pending-output.schema.json (renamed from the built gate-output, dropping the anyOf union) is the pending branch alone with ok, state and retry required by the relay rule. No script needed the union.

delivery-data's ok is defined as 'the command ran and reached a state': false only for refused, checkout_dirty and a command failure; merged, awaiting_merge, ci_failed, conflict and review_stale are ok, so the delivery repair loop runs. story-deliver.md lists the ok value of every state; story.js's !d.ok first test now behaves as designed.

Split (CATCHUP-R3). Fixed: the survey part (20 required fields) and the story-unit part (32 required fields) of the relay rule, held by relayed_outputs_require_every_property in tools/check.py and the schema fixtures. Left-for-builder: release-result.schema.json — the release-workflow package must type ok, state, version and tag and require all four; no release script exists at slice depth.
where: next/plugins/vsdd-factory/schemas/survey.schema.json; next/plugins/vsdd-factory/schemas/story-unit.schema.json; next/tools/check.py relayed_outputs_require_every_property; release-result part: the release-workflow package

what_was_done: review_rules is a required story-unit field in the delivered schema (empty when the project has none), so every command that returns a unit carries it and no story reviewer is told 'Review rules: none' by absence.
Same closure as P3BLD-15: story-unit carries review_rules, and survey and story-unit both carry rounds_used, so wave.js can count earlier rounds; fixtures prove the shapes validate.

Partly settled now: delivery-data.schema.json defines changed_files ('the files changed from reviewed_sha to the delivered head', the definition the finding proposes), so the schema half is done. Still left for the builder: the repaired list comes from the green gate's --since result, which no built command computes yet; the G-package that builds gate green and the story-deliver tool must take the same definition and add the conformance fixture with a repair that touches a new file.

Settled by dropping the condition (CATCHUP-R17): topics/verdicts.md's covering rule now ties the loops of a unit to one another by their recorded order and subject alone, and says that no review pass stores the commit the loop before it converged on, so the covering condition reads none. The alternative — carrying the from-commit in the review-step identity and step-result.schema.json — was not taken.

The rename is done in the spec, which is where the record lives at slice depth: step-record.schema.json's hook-added head is now worktree_head (one key, one meaning, beside the step result's head), rules/step-results.md and records/step.md name it, and store_step's signature in the schema description follows. The S3 package builds the record to this shape.

Consolidated: records/baseline.md now states the flaky-inherited-test rule once, worded per BLUEPRINT.md#4.13 ('an inherited test that fails and then passes when the gate runs the suite once more'); gate-green.md, workflows/ingest.md and packaging/tests-python.md link to it instead of restating it in the two wordings; conflicts/records-repair.md RR10's Used line names the blueprint's wording; and gate-result.schema.json and wave-gate-data.schema.json describe flaky with a pointer to record:baseline instead of '(section 2.9.8)'.

Does not arise at slice depth: no green gate command exists yet, so test_output cannot be added to a measured result. The G-package building gate green must add test_output to the gate result and story.js must refresh it with the patch.

The contradiction is settled by the amendment, which the built judge() now follows: grounded === false makes a finding not hard (f.grounded !== false in the hard test), and holdout keeps its blueprint-4.10 exemption from the location and grounding conditions. Universal test 14 fails without the grounded test (a critical ungrounded finding must land in advisory).

The spec's safe() literal admitted a leading dash; the built guard (first character alnum) does not. topics/prelude.md now carries the built regex, so a typed identifier can never become a vsdd option.

No drift remains: the amended topic states the names-gated grammar (a key=value word counts only for the workflow's own argument names), which the built ^([a-z_-]+)= implements exactly; every documented input, hyphenated keys included, parses identically, and universal test 12 pins both argument forms.

Does not arise at slice depth as a survey key: the built step() consults the platform's budget object (budget.total and remaining(), exercised by the harness-realm test) with TOKEN_FLOOR as the reserve, so no tokens_left limit key is needed for the toys. The limits-table owner must still decide whether tokens_left joins tables/limits.toml for real runs.
RUN.limits and LIMIT_KEYS carry gate_minutes: 60 and ci_minutes: 30, so every real survey key is known and universal test 9 (an unknown limit key fails the run) checks something.
Same closure as P3BLD-20, in tables/limits.toml's prelude names: gate_minutes and ci_minutes are known limit keys, enforced by the unknown-key check.

build-step.md now states the order (build.py regenerates the two marked sub-blocks inside workflow-lib/prelude.js first, then stamps the assembled file) and that the 400-line cap is measured after the generated sub-blocks are stripped, which is exactly what check.py's _strip_region measures.

The cap is now checked against the fair measure (generated sub-blocks excluded) and the delivered schemas moved out of the hand-written region, so the prelude sits well under 400 real lines with every mandated function; the platform-constraints check passes.

The marker-guard sentence in build-step.md now names the exact scan scope the build enforces (the toy workflows' stamped regions, and the build's own sources and tests quoting the markers), replacing the unguarded 'no file outside <plugin>/workflows/'.

Same closure as SL1-25: the guard's allowed files are named in the spec and implemented in build.py's allowed set (toys, harness, universal test, lint tests, tools), so --check holds as written against those files.

Test 3's spec text now states the interim rule the built test implements: every agentType is a roster agent via the generated ROLE table until <plugin>/agents/ is populated, after which file existence is checked.

Verified as amended: the topic's 4/5/7 preamble states the survey stub passes with ok true, every precondition met and the units the test supplies, which is what the built test 7 does; the run ends at the checkpoint (node suite green).

Verified as built: the relay assertions match 'checkpoint' rather than 'vsdd checkpoint', correct for any project_dir a stub supplies; the node suite passes including test 7 and the close-relay tests.
Verified as built: launch.sh's POSIX case guard (case "$0" in */*) here="${0%/*}";; *) here=. ;; esac) survives a bare-name invocation; the launcher suites pass under sh, bash and dash.

Verified as built: interpreter_ok's probe runs with its own writable UV_CACHE_DIR under the user's cache, so a broken uv cache cannot be misreported as a missing Python; the read-only-cache test asserts the uv_unusable message.

Verified as built: the uniform exit mapping (0->0, 10->2, other codes through fail()'s brief/notify arms) is what launch.sh does and what the test matrix asserts, with the mapping comment citing the design skeleton.

Verified as built: an unknown hook mode fails closed with exit 2 and a message (TestUnknownMode), and the failure table's missing rc-13 row is covered by the launcher's explicit 13 case (defence in depth for hook.py's floor check).

Verified as built: on rc 2 the launcher discriminates with uv python find --no-python-downloads '>=3.11' (uv_unusable with upgrade advice when an interpreter is found, py_floor otherwise), and the message/exit matrix is asserted per interpreter.
